findings.reason: Lock br->multicast_lock (spin_lock_init at net/bridge/br_multicast.c:1748) is shared between TIMER_SOFTIRQ callbacks and process-context code with the process side missing the bottom-half disable - the timer-softirq analogue of the seed's missing spin_lock_bh. TIMER-SOFTIRQ SIDE (all plain spin_lock, verified by grep in s12): br_multicast_group_expired (def 224, lock 230, setup_timer at 623), br_multicast_port_group_expired (def 285, lock 290, setup_timer at 650), br_multicast_router_expired (def 742, lock 747, setup_timer at 887), br_multicast_querier_expired (def 763, lock 766; wired by setup_timer at 1751/1756), br_multicast_query_expired (def 1698, lock 1701, setup_timer at 1753/1758) plus the ip4/ip6 port-query wrappers (setup_timer at 889/892); these execute in call_timer_fn from TIMER_SOFTIRQ. PROCESS SIDE (same lock object, plain spin_lock): br_multicast_enable_port (def 911, lock 915) and br_multicast_disable_port (def 928, lock 934) which walks port->mglist deleting port groups and deleting timers under the lock - reached from bridge STP port enable/disable, bridge start/stop and netlink/sysfs port-state configuration. UNTRUSTED SOURCE: attacker-influenced concurrency, not data - multicast group/port-group expiry, router-querier timeouts and query-interval ticks are timer-driven (influenced by remote IGMP/MLD traffic and locally triggered port-state changes); any of these expiring on the same CPU as a preempted process-context holder aligns both sides. COUNTEREVIDENCE CHECKED: sibling process-context sites of the very same lock use spin_lock_bh (1798, 1817, 1832, 1924, 1967), proving mixed discipline and that the plain sites are the defect; the del_timer() calls inside disable_port's critical section (940-944) do NOT wait for a callback already executing (del_timer does not synchronize), so the window stays open. UNSAFE USE: a TIMER_SOFTIRQ firing on the same CPU between a holder's spin_lock and spin_unlock spins forever on multicast_lock while the preempted holder can never resume -> soft lockup, RCU stall, bridge multicast control stall, repeatable local/remote-triggerable DoS. Same bug family confirmed in sibling snapshots s07 (f015) and s11 (f018); medium confidence because the process-context callers of enable/disable_port were established from the standard bridge call model plus the s12 registration sites, not line-level tracing.

Lock object struct iscsi_session.lock (this kernel generation's name for the lock the s05 sibling fact f016 calls frwd_lock) is shared between TIMER_SOFTIRQ callback bodies and BH-enabled process context with several plain spin_lock acquisitions and no _bh at those sites. TIMER-SOFTIRQ SIDE: iscsi_tmf_timedout (def drivers/scsi/libiscsi.c:1746, plain spin_lock(&session->lock) at 1751, wired via conn->tmf_timer.function = iscsi_tmf_timedout at 1779) and iscsi_check_transport_timeouts (def 2030, plain spin_lock(&session->lock) at 2036, wired via conn->transport_timer.function = iscsi_check_transport_timeouts at 2856) both run in call_timer_fn from TIMER_SOFTIRQ. PROCESS SIDE (holder): iscsi_eh_cmd_timed_out (def 1896, plain spin_lock(&session->lock) at 1910) is the scsi_host_template .eh_timed_out hook (installed at 2551-2552: shost->transportt->eh_timed_out = iscsi_eh_cmd_timed_out) invoked from the block-layer timeout work in process/kworker context with BH enabled. UNTRUSTED SOURCE: any iSCSI command timeout on the session plus the per-connection transport timer (fires every few seconds per conn) aligning on the same CPU; command timeouts are influenced by remote target behavior. COUNTEREVIDENCE CHECKED: many sibling sites of the same lock correctly use spin_lock_bh(&session->lock) (538, 794, 1326, 1354, 1603, 1774, 1803, 2099, 2170, 2238, 2278, 2301, 2329, 2358, 2401, 2441, 2864, 2908, 2944, 2989, 3057, 3081, 3104, 3135), so the plain sites 1751/1910/2036 are the discipline gap; whether any of the plain process-side callers already runs with BH disabled was not dynamically verified (medium confidence). UNSAFE USE: a timer softirq preempting eh_timed_out between lock and unlock spins forever on session->lock while the holder can never resume -> soft lockup/RCU stall and iSCSI LUN I/O stall DoS, the exact timer-branch shape reported for s05 (fact f016).

br_multicast_enable_port (def 911) takes the same br->multicast_lock with plain spin_lock at 915; second process-side site of finding 1; sibling process sites 1798/1817/1832/1924/1967 use spin_lock_bh.

Plain spin_lock(&session->lock) at 1910 inside iscsi_eh_cmd_timed_out (def 1896; .eh_timed_out hook installed at 2551-2552), i.e. BH-enabled process context, vs timer-softirq callbacks taking the same lock at 1751/2036; reported as finding 2.
Timer-side site of finding 2: iscsi_tmf_timedout (def 1746, conn->tmf_timer.function wired at 1779) takes plain spin_lock(&session->lock) at 1751 in TIMER_SOFTIRQ context.
Timer-side site of finding 2: iscsi_check_transport_timeouts (def 2030, conn->transport_timer.function wired at 2856) takes plain spin_lock(&session->lock) at 2036 in TIMER_SOFTIRQ context.

limitations: The full-tree timer-callback enumeration (timer_list/hrtimer/delayed_work bodies containing plain spin_lock) was not executed for s12 before the finalize order; only the two known sibling timer-branch bug families - net/bridge/br_multicast.c (br->multicast_lock) and drivers/scsi/libiscsi.c (session->lock) - were line-verified in this session via grep/sed.

Unresolved candidates (drivers/net/tun.c, net/802/garp.c, net/802/mrp.c, drivers/net/ethernet/broadcom/bcm63xx_enet.c, hostap hostap_ap.c ap_handle_timer, cxgb4 sge.c ptp_lock, iwlwifi pcie/tx.c txq stuck timer, qdisc sch_pie/sch_sfq/sch_red perturbation timers) were carried from sibling-snapshot rankings and were not verified in s12; their line numbers are unknown in this tree.

Static source analysis only: no compile, lockdep run, or runtime reproducer (the s12 tree has no top-level Makefile/.config); the process-context callers of br_multicast_enable_port/disable_port (br_stp_enable_port/br_stp_disable_port from netlink/sysfs port-state change and bridge start/stop) and the block-layer timeout work -> scsi eh_timed_out chain rest on standard kernel wiring plus the grep-visible registration sites (libiscsi.c:2551-2552), not line-level tracing in this session - reflected in medium confidence.

For both findings, the deadlock additionally requires the timer softirq to fire on the same CPU while the process-context holder is between lock and unlock; for libiscsi, whether any plain process-side caller already runs with BH disabled was not dynamically verified.
